name: Caupedactylus
sum: Large crested tapejarine from the Romualdo Formation (Albian) of the Araripe Basin, Brazil.
wsnote: Estimated by Kellner at 3.3 m — the largest known tapejarine.
holotype: MN 4726-V — Romualdo Formation, Araripe Basin, NE Brazil.
material: Partial skeleton with an almost complete skull (~46 cm), lower jaws and partial postcranium.
exceptional: Acid-prepared, three-dimensional skull with well-preserved palate.
biology: Toothless, downturned beak and a large, very thin head crest. Tapejarines are generally considered omnivores or plant-eaters.
author: Kellner 2013
